premiseChanged: The MDM commodity integration is live, so the 9 October afternoon ruling's blanket 'wait until commodities come from MDM' no longer holds for most of this theme. reference-data serves GET /commodities from MDM's product search (referencedata origin/main:src/main/java/uk/gov/defra/trade/imports/commodities/CommoditySearchService.java:48), the animals frontend reads it (frontend origin/main:src/server/app/sets/live-animals/services/commodities/client.js:7-16), and the catalogue now reaches 26 selectable chapter-01 codes rather than five stub commodities. Three of the four blocked rows (inc-013, inc-019, inc-023) lose their only reason to wait. rows.verdict: dropped — see correctionApplied; the verdict below was the superseded first pass
rows.evidence: MDM data half of the block is gone. reference-data returns commodity groups from MDM's product search, keeping only rows MDM does not flag isGerminal (CommoditySearchService.java:43, :81-:88, :103). The frontend's stub-mode fixture, captured from that path, holds 26 selectable chapter-01 codes (frontend origin/main:src/server/app/services/_capture/fixtures/commodities.json): 0101, 0102, 0103, 010410, 010420, 01051111, 01051200, 01051300, 01051400, 01051500, 01059400, 01059910, 01059920, 01059930, 01059950, 01061410, 01061490, 01061900, 01062000, 01063100, 01063200, 01063300, 01063910, 01063980, 01064100, 01064900. Criterion 1 is therefore largely reachable, but not as written: every code DR2.1 names at 6 digits MDM serves at 8 (Chicken is 01051111 and 01059400, not 010511; Turkey 01051200 and 01059930; Duck 01051300 and 01059910; Goose 01051400 and 01059920; Guinea fowl 01051500 and 01059950; Rabbit 01061410 and 01061490; Parrot 01063200; Ostrich 01063300; Reptile 01062000), and Camel is absent altogether - there is no 010613 or 01061300 anywhere in MDM's chapter-01 tree and no Camelus species in the capture (stub origin/main:src/main/resources/responses/mdmProductSearchResponses.json, the '010' search, 49 commodity rows). MDM also adds four codes DR2.1 does not list: Birds of prey 01063100, Pigeons 01063910, other birds 01063980 and other insects 01064900. Criterion 2 (0102 named 'Cattle') is unmet and cannot be met from MDM as integrated: reference-data's CommodityGroup carries only code and species (referencedata origin/main:.../CommodityGroup.java:13-16) and CommoditySpecies only latinName and commonName (CommoditySpecies.java:15-20), so the frontend has no name to show and renders the bare code everywhere - legendFor is the identity function on the code (frontend origin/main:src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/commodities/search/view-model/labels.js:1), used by the result groups (view-model/commodity-groups.js:19), the selected panel (view-model/selected-summary.js:18) and, through buildCommodityGroups, by Commodity details, where heading is the code (features/commodities/view-model/commodity-groups.js:6). MDM's commodity rows do carry a description, but it is CN tariff text, not a name a trader would recognise: 0102 is 'Live bovine animals', 0101 'Live horses, asses, mules and hinnies', 0103 'Live swine', 01061900 'Other', 01061490 'other than. 0106 14 10', 01063980 'other than  0105; 010631; 010632 and 01063910' and 01051111 'Weighing not more than 185 g:Fowls of the species Gallus domesticus, Grandparent and parent female chicks: Laying stocks'. Nor can it express DR2.1's four-way split of 01061900 into Cat, Dog, Ferret and Other live mammals: that is one CN code described as 'Other'. The rename half of criterion 2 is in any case moot - 'Cow' has gone from the frontend, leaving one stale doc example (src/server/app/model/obligations/README.md:100), and the tests now assert the Latin name instead (tests origin/main:tests/animals/e2e/pages/consignment-details.spec.ts:91-92). Criteria 3 and 4 are superseded by the catalogue invariant that MDM's entries win: MDM lists 15 species under 0102, not DR2.1's 11, with different names and two elephants among them (Elephas maximus, Loxodonta africana), and oddities of its own ('Animals' as Poephagus spp.'s common name, lower-case 'water buffalos'); under 0101 it lists five, not three, misspelling caballus as 'cabalus' and carrying two unnamed mule rows ('Eq cabalus*asinus', 'Equus cabalus*asinus') plus Equus zebra. Criterion 5 is half met in the data and not at all on the page: MDM holds Felis catus 'Domestic Cat' and Canis familiaris 'Dog' (not 'Domestic dog'), but no page shows a common name, because speciesLabel returns the Latin name alone (frontend origin/main:src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/commodities/species-label.js:1). Criterion 6's ferret half is met: Mustela putorius furo is in MDM with common name 'Ferret' and is already in the permanent-address list beside cat and dog (frontend origin/main:src/server/app/sets/live-animals/services/commodities/rules.js:62-69); its Other live mammals half is reachable (Aepyceros 'Impala' through Xenarthra 'edentate' are all in MDM's 01061900) except the single 'Other Mammalia' entry, which MDM does not hold. Criterion 7's second half is met and its first half is undeliverable: MDM returns an empty result for 'fish' (stub mdmProductSearchResponses.json, the 'fish' search, totalElements 0) and serves no chapter-03 code, so Fish (0301) is indeed no longer offered but Ornamental fish (030111) cannot be offered either. Criterion 8 ('every species name reads exactly as DR2.1 gives it') is flatly contradicted by the invariant that a search box's entries are what MDM serves. Criterion 9 is built, and built the other way round: PACKAGE_COUNT_CODES holds 23 codes (rules.js:37-60) including every poultry code, rabbit 01061410, reptile 01062000, birds of prey 01063100, parrot 01063200, other birds 01063980, bees 01064100 and other insects 01064900 - precisely the commodities DR2.1 says must not be asked - while omitting 01061490, 01063300 and 01063910. Criterion 11 is met on main: the k6 suite already searches 'Bos taurus' (perftests origin/main:src/config/test-data.js:5), and MDM returns nothing for 'cow' (stub mdmProductSearchResponses.json, the 'cow' search, totalElements 0), so the move off 'Cow' has happened.
rows.proposedChange: Keep the row, unblock nothing yet, and split it. Drop criterion 11 (met on main) and criterion 8 (contradicted by the MDM invariant). Restate criterion 1 against MDM's real 8-digit codes, naming the two codes each kind of poultry and rabbit has, and adding the four codes MDM serves that DR2.1 does not list, so the catalogue is described as MDM gives it. Restate criteria 3, 4, 5 and 6 as 'the species MDM lists under the code, by its own names', keeping only the behaviour DR2.1 settles - that cat, dog and ferret need a permanent address and Other live mammals does not - and drop the hand-written species lists, which are now a snapshot of a worse source than the live one. Keep criterion 7's second half as a regression check that no fish is offered, and drop its first half. Leave criterion 2 on the row as the one thing that still blocks it, and record three open questions for Sam rather than guessing: (1) where a trader-facing commodity name comes from, given MDM serves only CN tariff text - a service-owned name table over the CN codes, MDM's description cleaned up, or the code alone as main ships today; (2) whether DR2.1's split of 01061900 into Cat, Dog, Ferret and Other live mammals survives, since MDM cannot express it and main instead renders 01061900 one row per species (PER_SPECIES_CODE, rules.js:112); (3) whether camel and ornamental fish are dropped from the catalogue or chased with the MDM team, since neither is in the GBN-AG dataset. Move criterion 9 to its own new row with its own ruling question, because main's package list is not a gap but a contradiction - someone chose the opposite rule, and the backlog should not quietly overwrite it. Correct the row's second note: main no longer keys the unweaned list on the name 'Cow'; UNWEANED_CODES is keyed on the code 0102 (rules.js:78), so the rename does not endanger it. Correct the third note: commodities.commodityLabel no longer exists, the heading seam is legendFor plus buildCommodityGroups, and of the tests it lists only the tests repo's consignment-details.spec.ts still touches this ground, now asserting 'Bos taurus'. Keep the row blocked, but say in the open question that it waits on a design decision, not on MDM.

rows.evidence: The row's only stated block was MDM, and MDM is live. Nothing else it asks for is on main. Results are not sorted: reference-data preserves MDM's order through a LinkedHashMap (referencedata origin/main:.../CommoditySearchService.java:146-152) and the frontend groups them in encounter order (frontend origin/main:.../search/view-model/commodity-groups.js:17-19), and the tests repo asserts that order deliberately - 'groups the matching species under their commodity code, in reference-data's order' (tests origin/main:tests/animals/e2e/pages/commodities.spec.ts:45). So criterion 1 will change an existing test, not fill a hole. No text is bolded: the checkbox items take speciesLabel, which is the plain Latin name (species-label.js:1). A bold-matching helper does exist, written for the type-aheads, with accent folding and a strong class (frontend origin/main:src/client/common/helpers/bold-matches.js), and a server-side escapeHtml sits in shared/escape-html.js, so criterion 2 should reuse both rather than add a third. The selected panel exists and is already grouped the right way, but with the wrong parts: selectedSummary groups the selection by commodity code and lists its species (view-model/selected-summary.js:11-21), and the template renders each group as a bold legend followed by the species joined with ', ' in a single list item (search/search.njk:66-73). So criterion 3's bold commodity line and species-per-commodity structure are half there, with the bare code where the name belongs; criterion 4 is absent entirely - there is no per-species remove control, only one 'Clear all' button (search.njk:74-79). Criterion 5 holds for what exists: the page is one form posting to itself, with Search and Clear as named submit buttons and no client-side behaviour, so the chips' remove buttons simply need to be submit buttons too. Criterion 6 still applies to the new strings.
rows.proposedChange: Set the row todo and drop both MDM open questions. Keep every criterion. Replace criterion 3's 'Cattle (0102):' example with the code, and add a note that the line shows whatever inc-012's naming decision settles on, so this row builds the chip and remove-button markup without waiting for the name. newRows.title: Which commodities ask for a number of packages follows one agreed list
newRows.why: Design Release 2.1 and main disagree outright, and the backlog should not silently overwrite a choice someone made. DR2.1 (inc-012 criterion 9) asks for a number of packages on Cattle, Horse, Pig, Sheep, Goat, Cat, Dog, Ferret and Other live mammals, and not on Chicken, Turkey, Duck, Goose, Guinea fowl, Rabbit, Camel, Ostrich, Parrot, Reptile, Bees or Ornamental fish. Main's PACKAGE_COUNT_CODES (frontend origin/main:src/server/app/sets/live-animals/services/commodities/rules.js:37-60) asks on 23 codes including every poultry code, rabbit 01061410, reptile 01062000, birds of prey 01063100, parrot 01063200, other birds 01063980, bees 01064100 and other insects 01064900 - the ones DR2.1 excludes - and omits 01061490, 01063300 and 01063910. The two lists are near-inverses on the bird and insect codes, so this is a ruling to get, not a gap to fill.
newRows.openQuestion: Which list is right - DR2.1's nine mammal commodities, main's 23 codes, or MDM's own packageType data, which the commodity rows carry and reference-data does not yet read? Until it is settled the hard stop in inc-018 makes the question required wherever it is asked, without deciding where that is.

newRows.title: Species read as their common name with the Latin name in brackets again
newRows.why: A regression came in with the MDM search. speciesLabel returns the Latin name alone (frontend origin/main:src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/commodities/species-label.js:1), so every page that lists a species - the commodity search checkboxes, the selected panel, Commodity details and the Selected commodities tables - shows 'Bos taurus' where it used to show 'Domestic cattle (Bos taurus)'. The frontend had delivered common-name-with-Latin-in-brackets under DR1 parity (frontend 949bb9d6, 'offer each species as its common name with the Latin name in brackets'), and the data is still there to do it: reference-data passes MDM's commonName through (referencedata origin/main:.../CommoditySpecies.java:15-20) and the frontend stores speciesCommonName on every line (.../search/selection/rows.js:7-24). The tests followed the regression rather than catching it (tests origin/main:tests/animals/e2e/pages/consignment-details.spec.ts:91-92 now assert 'Bos taurus'). inc-013 criterion 1 assumes the common-name label format, so it rests on this.
newRows.openQuestion: None. The label format is already settled by DR1 parity and DR2.1 alike; only the fallback needs stating, for the species where MDM holds no common name (Capreolus, Gazella, Elephas and many others are null in the capture), which DR2.1 gives as the commodity name with the Latin name in brackets.

newRows.title: The frontend's stub commodity fixture matches what the MDM stub serves
newRows.why: Two captures of the same MDM data disagree, so stub-mode and stack runs show different species names. The frontend's fixture was captured on 27 October with EUDPA-617 (frontend c3183a8e, src/server/app/services/_capture/fixtures/commodities.json) and gives Bos taurus the common name 'Cattle or Cow'. The stub service was corrected on 28 October to return 'Domestic Cattle' for 0102 (stub afb74c3, 'return Domestic Cattle as the 0102 common name') and recaptured from TST on 30 October (stub 5cf8a70), and now gives Bos taurus 'Domestic Cattle'. The frontend fixture was never recaptured, so it is three days behind the stub it is meant to mirror. Nothing fails today because no page shows a common name, but inc-025 makes the common name visible, at which point stub-mode tests and stack tests assert different words.
newRows.openQuestion: None. Recapture the frontend fixture from the current stub and add a check that keeps the two in step, so the next MDM recapture cannot leave them apart again.

inFlightTickets.title: Save commodity name, code and type for each commodity on a notification
inFlightTickets.doesItUnblockInc012: No. It makes the gap matter more and partly entrenches it. The branch is rebased on main and so is live against MDM, and it does fix the downstream half this theme never owned: a notification now persists commodities[] with a per-entry name, CN code, description, totals and type, and each species carries MDM's commonName, which the backend passes to PIMS as the trade line description and common name (backend #115: 'TradeLineItem uses description (commodity) and commonName (species), not commodity display name alone'). But it does not supply the commodity names inc-012 criterion 2 needs. It adds two hard-coded tables to the frontend (frontend fix/EUDPA-669-commodity-name-code-type:src/server/app/sets/live-animals/services/commodities/index.js:18-31): COMMODITY_DESCRIPTIONS covers 4 of the catalogue's 26 codes, commented 'MDM commodity descriptions (reference-data /commodities?codes=); stubbed until live lookup', and COMMODITY_NAMES_BY_CODE covers 3 - '0101': 'Horse', '0102': 'Cow', '0301': 'Fish'. The mapper reads name: commodityNameFor(code) ?? code (mapper-a/commodity.js:27), so for 23 of 26 codes the commodity name sent downstream and shown on both dashboards is the bare CN code, and the branch's own doc says so: 'A notification sends its first line's CN code (for example 0102) as commodity.name, until reference-data supplies commodity names' (sets/live-animals/docs/services.md). Worse for this theme, it pins 'Cow' for 0102 in code and in the tests repo, where domain/animals/constants/commodity-names.ts is exactly { '0102': 'Cow', '01061900': '01061900' }. That is the behaviour inc-012 criterion 2 exists to change, now with a test locking it. It also includes '0301' Fish, which MDM does not serve at all.
inFlightTickets.doesItUnblockInc024: No, and it argues the other way. PACKAGE_COUNT_CODES is unchanged on the branch. Its doc offers a rationale for main's list - 'The package-count list holds the codes of the design's package-count list that MDM's live-animal data holds. Where the design named an entry by animal, the whole code is on the list' - which explains including 01061900 (one code covering cat, dog, ferret and other mammals) but does not explain including the poultry codes, 01062000, 01063100, 01063200, 01063980, 01064100 or 01064900, which Design Release 2.1 names individually as commodities that must not be asked. So inc-024's ruling is still needed, and there is now a doc asserting a rationale that does not cover the disputed codes.
inFlightTickets.doesItFixInc025: No. speciesLabel and legendFor are both unchanged on the branch (verified by diff against origin/main). So the species common name is now stored on every line and sent downstream, while the trader still sees the bare Latin name. inc-025 remains to build, and its data source is now doubly confirmed.
inFlightTickets.defectFound: The branch drops the domestic dog from the permanent-address rule and puts the raccoon dog in its place. PERMANENT_ADDRESS_SPECIES for 01061900 changes from ['Felis catus', 'Canis familiaris', 'Canis lupus familiaris', 'Mustela putorius furo'] to ['Felis catus', 'Nyctereutes procyonoides', 'Mustela putorius furo'] (frontend fix/EUDPA-669-commodity-name-code-type:src/server/app/sets/live-animals/services/commodities/rules.js:62-69). MDM holds both species under 01061900: 'Canis familiaris' with the common name 'Dog', and 'Nyctereutes procyonoides' with the common name 'Raccoon Dog'. So as the branch stands a trader importing a dog is no longer asked for the animal's permanent address, and one importing a raccoon dog is. Dropping 'Canis lupus familiaris' is defensible - MDM does not hold it - but dropping 'Canis familiaris' is not. The branch's own doc contradicts its code in one paragraph: it says 01061900 'holds the domestic cats, dogs and ferrets that need one' and then that 'Nyctereutes procyonoides (MDM's raccoon dog) is listed for the permanent-address gate'. The likely cause is visible in the tests repo, where the fixture is named for what it is and found by the wrong search term: raccoonDog: { searchTerm: 'dog', commodityCode: '01061900', latinName: 'Nyctereutes procyonoides' } (ins-tests fix/EUDPA-669-commodity-name-code-type:domain/animals/constants/commodity-lines.ts:12). No test catches it: the permanent-address journey is exercised only with domesticCat (Felis catus) in MANDATORY_COMMODITY_LINES and ALL_COMMODITY_LINES, and the raccoonDog fixture carries no permanentAddress answer, so the suite stays green with the dog gone. This breaks inc-012's restated criterion 4 and is a live defect on an open pull request, not a backlog matter.

inFlightTickets.title: Add a search type-ahead for choosing commodities, reusable across the journey
inFlightTickets.doesItUnblockInc013: Not as it stands: there is nothing in flight. Every pull request was closed unmerged on 23 October and the branch no longer exists on the remote, four days before EUDPA-617 landed the MDM search and rewrote the whole feature. Jira still says In Dev, so the work is expected to resume, but it would be a fresh build rather than a rebase. The closed diff is still worth quarrying (frontend #425, +1026/-235): it was green on E2E, Lighthouse and the Sonar gate, and it built a reusable live-search macro and client module outside the commodities feature, a GET .../commodities/results route rendering the same _results.njk partial the page uses, and emphasis done properly - matching.js reporting the ranges it matched and the template rendering them as <strong>, with no HTML built in JavaScript.
inFlightTickets.overlapWithInc013: Partial, and only on the JavaScript side. EUDPA-616 delivers inc-013's criterion 2 (matched text in bold) and part of criterion 3 (a selected panel) as a progressive enhancement, and its own acceptance criteria keep the server-rendered search-then-tick-boxes flow unchanged as the no-JavaScript fallback. inc-013 needs more than that: criterion 1 (results sorted alphabetically) and criterion 4 (a remove button per species chip) are not in EUDPA-616 at all, and inc-013 criterion 5 requires the chips' remove buttons and Clear all to work by posting the page, which a JavaScript-only enhancement does not satisfy. So the two are complements, not substitutes: inc-013 owns the server-rendered behaviour and EUDPA-616 the enhancement over it. Whichever is built second should reuse the other's matching and emphasis rather than add a second copy - note that main already carries a bold-matching helper for the type-aheads (src/client/common/helpers/bold-matches.js).
inFlightTickets.staleness: EUDPA-616's ticket text predates the MDM integration and says so: its tech notes read 'This ticket builds the search against the existing (stub) commodity catalogue. A follow-up ticket is needed to pull commodity codes from MDM as the real data source, replacing the current static/stub list.' That follow-up was EUDPA-617, which has landed. The ticket also describes the page as printing 'the whole commodity catalogue as fixed checkbox fieldsets on load', which has not been true since design snagging. It should be re-read against main before it is picked up again.

correctionApplied.what: This re-analysis's first pass kept inc-012 blocked on a commodity-naming question and called camel and ornamental fish a 'data gap' to chase with the MDM team. Both were wrong, and inc-012 is now dropped.
correctionApplied.why: Two things were missed. First, provenance: every criterion behind the named catalogue traces to claims of kind 'data' extracted from the prototype's own hard-coded demo files at commit 04a073b - app/data/commodities.js:10-25 for the commodity names ('Cattle', 'Pig'), app/data/commodities-0102-species.js:3-15 for the 11 cattle species. They are a designer's stand-in data for a catalogue that did not exist yet, not a statement of requirement. The prototype's declared role in sources.json covers 'every page, field, option, hint, error message, branch and journey step'; a reference list's contents are not in that set. Second, the governing ruling: claim 25 of ruling:sam-2026-10-09 says every reference list 'is built now against reference-data as it is, and its content is what MDM serves. Where a list's content differs from Design Release 2.1, that is MDM's content to change, never a reason to block a row or edit a list in code.' Claim 28 of ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm carved commodities out of that only 'until commodities come from MDM', and said that once they did, 'the area is re-distilled'. They came on 27 October, so the carve-out expired and claim 25 governs. Claim 2 of the same ruling says it again for search boxes: 'List entries: they are whatever MDM serves through reference-data', with only 'how the list reads' following the prototype, and then only 'wherever the component can show them' - so a label MDM does not serve is not a requirement the prototype can create.
effect: inc-012 is dropped, not blocked. Its criteria were list content, which is MDM's.

Camel and ornamental fish are not a data gap and never blocked anything. Fish is correct as it stands: live aquatic animals are not a GBN-AG live-animal commodity and fish is managed under the IUU regime, not this service. Camel is a content request to MDM if anyone wants it.
MDM's data-quality oddities block nothing and are not this programme's work to fix in code - claim 25 is explicit that a list's content is never a reason to edit a list in code.

inc-024 survives, because which commodities are asked a question is a service rule rather than list content - but its framing changed from 'DR2.1 and main contradict each other' to 'is main's rule right?', since the DR2.1 side is the same demo data.

inc-013, inc-019, inc-023, inc-025 and inc-026 are unaffected. inc-013 is how the list reads and behaves, which does follow the prototype. inc-025 is a label format over a field MDM does serve (commonName). inc-019 and inc-023 needed only that poultry and pig reach the catalogue, which they have. inc-026 is test hygiene.
correctionApplied.lesson: A claim extracted from a prototype with kind 'data' is a fixture, not a requirement. Where a row's criteria rest on such claims and a ruling assigns that data to another system, the row is a candidate to drop rather than to rewrite. Worth a check in the distil method: list-content criteria sourced only from kind 'data' prototype claims should be challenged against claim 25 before they reach a row.

deferred: Content request to MDM, blocking nothing: camel is absent from MDM's GBN-AG chapter-01 tree (no 010613 or 01061300). Only needed if the business wants camels importable as live animals. Under claim 25 this is MDM's content, never a reason to block a row.

No action: ornamental fish and fish generally are absent from MDM and correct to be absent. Live aquatic animals are not a GBN-AG live-animal commodity, and fish is managed under the IUU regime rather than this service. The prototype's 'Ornamental fish' entry was demo data.

Content requests to MDM, blocking nothing: MDM spells the horse 'Equus cabalus' and the mule 'Eq cabalus*asinus', missing an l in caballus, and carries a second unnamed mule row; it lists two elephants under 0102 (live bovine animals); it gives Poephagus spp. the common name 'Animals' and Bubalus the lower-case 'water buffalos'. These reach the receiving service as the GBN-AG scientific name, so they are worth raising, but claim 25 makes them MDM's content to change and explicitly not a reason to edit a list in code. c-014's ruling to correct Design Release 2.1's misspellings is spent: the list it referred to is gone.

Design question, blocking nothing: the commodity heading in the journey is the bare CN code (for example '0102'), because reference-data carries no commodity name and MDM holds none in any field - its commodity rows carry CN tariff text ('Live bovine animals', 'Other', 'other than. 0106 14 10'), and animalSubcategory, natureOfCommodity and breedCategory are empty on all 49 rows in the capture. Is a CN code good enough for a trader, and if not, should MDM serve names or should the service hold its own name table over the CN codes? For designers, with Sam. Note the stakes rose with EUDPA-669, which sends that value downstream to PIMS as the trade line description for 23 of the 26 codes.
